verdict.rationale: Rive documents multiple ways to drive it programmatically: open-source runtime APIs for embedding/controlling animations (rive-docs-21, rive-gh-1), RML as a text-based file format for coding-agent workflows (rive-docs-13, rive-docs-20, rive-docs-25), and an official MCP server confirmed live via keyless fetch that exposes editor tools (create/manage files, shapes, state machines, data binding, scripts) to AI agents (rive-docs-19, rive-probe-4, rive-probe-rt-2). This directly satisfies an AI-native user's need to drive the product via documented public interfaces rather than only a GUI. Missing for 10: a conventional REST/OpenAPI-style API (probed endpoints all 404, rive-probe-3), and independent/community corroboration of successful AI-agent-driven API usage beyond first-party docs.
